title: Compact pivot panels and chart overscroll heuristics for Console cost & rollout surfaces
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Cost Explorer and Rollouts pages suffer inconsistent scroll/overscroll behavior and modal stacking across Chrome, Safari (both WebKit variants) and legacy Edge. Large cost pivot panels can push charts off-canvas on smaller viewports; users lose context when keyboard-traversing modals due to pointer/scroll handoff differences between browsers. Goal: design a resilient layout system that preserves context for cost pivoting and rollout comparisons, provides graceful chart rendering fallbacks, and harmonizes modal stacking/gesture behavior across major browsers without regressing performance.
design_summary: Deliver a slot-based panel layout that allows compact pivoting (left rail collapses to a narrow slot on narrow viewports, pivots expand in-place) plus an overscroll heuristic for charts that uses a small visual anchor (mini-sparkline) and progressive reveal. Introduce a modal slot-layer (z-safe regions) to avoid z-index fights with browser-specific stacking contexts. Provide SVG -> Canvas -> PNG fallback chain for heavy charts on Safari/old Edge and add pointer/keyboard interaction harmonization for touch devices.
acceptance_criteria: Pivot panels collapse to a 56px slot at <960px and expand inline without triggering global reflow beyond a threshold
Charts preserve 80% of data context (minimap + focused area) when pivoting happens or when modal opens on top
Modal slot-layer prevents keyboard focus from escaping and avoids z-index regressions in Safari stacking contexts
SVG charts have a deterministic fallback to Canvas on Safari 15/16 and to server-rendered PNG for customers with heavy tokenized datasets
Cross-browser QA matrix shows consistent overscroll bounce/elasticity behavior across Chrome, Safari mobile, iOS Safari, Firefox, and Edge (desktop)
Accessibility: keyboard-only navigation can open/close pivots and modals; screen reader announces pivot state and chart focus
Perf: initial page TTI impact < 120ms for console surfaces in development environment with 10k tokenized cost rows
implementation_notes: Engineering to expose a lightweight CSS slot component (slot-width, collapsed-width, expand-flow). For charts, implement layered rendering: primary SVG with requestAnimationFrame keyed lightweight updates; fallback hook that switches to offscreen canvas via OffscreenCanvas when WebKit reports paint thrash; final server PNG endpoint for extremely large datasets. Use a focus-sentinel pattern to trap keyboard focus inside modal-slot-layer. Provide a feature flag `slot_panel_v1` for gradual rollout and A/B measurement on resource usage.
tradeoffs_and_decisions:
- Chosen slot-based approach over full panel flyouts to avoid frequent reflow on narrow viewports (improves perceived latency).
- Prefer conservative fallback order (SVG -> Canvas -> PNG) to maintain interactivity where possible.
- Decided against aggressive virtualization of charts for this iteration to reduce complexity; deferred to follow-up ticket (ENG-32910).
- Accessibility-first: added explicit ARIA live region announcements for pivot open/close states even though it slightly increases DOM size.
risks: Safari paint thrash on older macOS versions may still show jank for extremely wide charts
Server-side PNG fallback increases bandwidth for affected sessions — needs rate-limiting and caching
Complexity of slot-layer could interact with third-party browser extensions that rewrite DOM ordering
